--- title: "Building the Analytic Files" format: html --- In this syntax, we'll import all of the Dallas County files provided and create two analytic files based on the templates in the second and third tabs here: https://csgorg.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/Team-JC-Research-JJ_AV/EZ-RDTetlZVCoiQxlasiboEBhsT7WNlx5v0qR7sDBji1-A?e=eggzRJ See `Codebooks` and `Data Diagram` tabs for more information on each individual data file. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ############################################# ### clean and de-dup child dataframe ### this is our base demo file for the sample ############################################# child_clean <- child %>% distinct(unique_id, .keep_all=TRUE) %>% ### no records dropped ### clean race/ethnicity and gender mutate(race_clean = case_when( race=="Asian or Pacific Islander" & ethnicity!="Hispanic" ~ 1, race=="Black" & ethnicity!="Hispanic" ~ 2, ethnicity=="Hispanic" ~ 3, race=="White" & ethnicity!="Hispanic" ~ 4, race %in% c("Unknown","American Indian or Alaskan Native") & ethnicity!="Hispanic" ~ 5, TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)), race_clean = factor(race_clean, levels = c(1,2,3,4,5), labels = c("Asian", "Black", "Hispanic", "White", "Other"))) %>% mutate(gender_clean = case_when( gender=="Female" ~ 1, gender=="Male" ~ 2, TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)), gender_clean = factor(gender_clean, levels = c(1,2), labels = c("Female", "Male"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` distinct: no rows removed ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` mutate: new variable 'race_clean' (factor) with 5 unique values and 0% NA ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` mutate: new variable 'gender_clean' (factor) with 2 unique values and 0% NA ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ######################################## ### clean and de-dup supervision dataframe ######################################## supervision_clean <- supervision %>% distinct(unique_id, referral_number, supervision_begin_date, .keep_all=TRUE) %>% ### 1 record dropped (note: 170 recods have duplicated IDs but different begin dates) ### clean dates and create years for potential grouping in future trend analysis mutate(supervision_begin_date = ymd(as_date(supervision_begin_date)), supervision_end_date = ymd(as_date(supervision_end_date)), supervision_begin_year = year(supervision_begin_date), supervision_end_year = year(supervision_end_date)) %>% ### create unique referral ID possible filtering, joining, or counting mutate(unique_referral_id = paste0(unique_id, referral_number)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` distinct: removed one row (<1%), 8,760 rows remaining ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` mutate: converted 'supervision_begin_date' from double to Date (0 new NA) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` converted 'supervision_end_date' from double to Date (0 new NA) ``` ::: ::: 'supervision_end_year' (integer) with 7 unique values and 9% NA ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` mutate: new variable 'unique_referral_id' (character) with 8,591 unique values and 0% NA ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ######################################## ### clean and de-dup offenses dataframe ######################################## offenses_clean <- offenses %>% distinct(unique_id, referral_number, offense_id, .keep_all=TRUE) %>% ### no records dropped ### clean dates and create years for potential grouping in future trend analysis mutate(offense_date = ymd(as_date(offense_date)), referral_date = ymd(as_date(referral_date)), disposition_date = ymd(as_date(excel_numeric_to_date(as.numeric(as.character(disposition_date)), date_system = "modern"))), offense_year = year(offense_date), referral_year = year(referral_date), disposition_year = year(disposition_date)) %>% ### create unique referral ID and unique offense ID for possible filtering or counting mutate(unique_referral_id = paste0(unique_id, referral_number), unique_offense_id = paste0(unique_id, referral_number, offense_id)) %>% ### calculate number of offenses per referral by grouping by unique_referral_id group_by(unique_referral_id) %>% mutate(unique_offenses_per_referral_count = n_distinct(unique_offense_id, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% ungroup() ``` ::: {.cell-output
